summary: Iter16 — Coming Soon launch gate: end-to-end tested BOTH backend and frontend. Backend: 8/8 pytest tests pass covering GET /api/site/settings (public defaults), POST /api/admin/site/settings (403 unauth, 200 with JWT, 200 with legacy X-Admin-Code), POST /api/organisations/{slug}/auth/login (200 with correct pw, 401 with wrong), /api/subscribe, /api/web-wizard/enquiry. Frontend: fresh unauth visitor sees ComingSoon at /, /events, /admin (gate works on all routes). All required data-testids present (cs-countdown + days/hours/mins/secs unit blocks, cs-subscribe-input/submit, cs-admin-login-open/dialog/email/password/submit, cs-org-login-open/dialog/slug/password/submit, cs-webwizard-open/dialog/wiz-name/email/details/submit). Subscribe → success toast; Wizard → toast 'Thanks — your Web Design Wizard enquiry has been sent' + dialog closes. Admin login from CS: dialog opens → creds accepted → dialog closes → CS unmounts → home-page renders → rn-admin-jwt + rn-role='admin' stored → PERSISTS across hard reload (CS stays hidden). Org login from CS: dialog opens → select blackrod-town-council → password → routed to /organisation-dashboard, org-dashboard visible, rn-role='org' + rn-org-tokens persist across reload. Admin site-mode-card toggle: badge flips 'Coming Soon' ↔ 'Public / Live', /api/site/settings.coming_soon flips accordingly. Final state left with coming_soon=true (launch-ready) as required.
critical_code_review_comments: Review request document referenced slug 'rodlife-events' for the org auth endpoint, but that slug does not exist in the seeded DB — it's the deployment subdomain. Test uses 'blackrod-town-council' which is the actual seeded org matching the frontend UI test. Main agent should correct the problem statement or seed 'rodlife-events' if that org is intended.
server.py still 3800+ lines; Admin.jsx still ~2300 lines — split recommended (carried from iter14/15).

ComingSoon.jsx has a legacy-code short-circuit that bypasses backend auth if REACT_APP_ADMIN_LAUNCH_CODE is present in the client env. This works but the launch code is bundled into the frontend JS, so it's discoverable by anyone. Consider removing legacy client-side path pre-launch, or at least documenting the risk.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all CS gate + login + wizard + subscribe + site-mode toggle flows pass)
